dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspected all graph files (sizes, format, node names) and the reference alignment; quantified that the reference alignment yields NC=1 but S3=0.248 — an explicit baseline measurement.

Evaluated multiple simple baselines (degree-rank, file-order, numeric-sort, degree-distribution matching) with computed S3/NC and reasoned they fall far short of thresholds, rather than committing blindly.
Recognized SANA as the published network-alignment tool designed to optimize S3, downloaded and built it — researching/selecting a known-reasonable approach with stated rationale.

Researched SANA's lock/color-file options to enforce yeast NC, explicitly identifying task-specific levers: topology drives S3, reference-seeding/locking drives NC, with differing constraints per deliverable.
Sustained analysis: tuned SANA runs, compared free (S3~0.518, NC~0) vs locked (S3~0.478, NC>0.3) results, deriving per-deliverable strategy grounded in measured scores.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized both network pairs, quantified baseline scores (reference NC=1/S3=0.248, degree-rank far below), researched and built the published SANA tool for S3 optimization, and identified the exact per-deliverable levers (topology for S3, reference-locking for NC) — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because it converged on a single published method (SANA) rather than evaluating multiple methods against instance sizes/runtime. The later collapse into a stuck terminal is an execution failure outside this dimension and does not lower the orientation quality already established.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Clear ordered pipeline: inspect formats (step 2) → parse graphs + copy yeast reference and compute validation/S3 (step 3) → baseline degree-rank alignments computing S3/NC (step 4). Scorer/evaluator built before optimizing, a hallmark of level-8 sequencing.

Treats the two deliverables distinctly with their numeric thresholds as done-criteria (DM-HS S3>=0.32 vs yeast S3>=0.55 & NC>=0.30), noting reference gives NC=1 but S3=0.248. Progresses baseline → degree-distribution matching → greedy multi-start as ordered sub-goals.

After adopting SANA, milestones remain explicit and gated on measured scores: short verification run → extract S3 → discover NC near-zero → design lock-file strategy sized to guarantee NC>0.31. Shows effort budgeting by difficulty (NC-constrained yeast vs S3-only fly) and fallback branches (lock/hybrid), touching level-10 elements.

Continued milestone gating on measured S3 (free 0.518, locked 0.478) with explicit fallback plans: cooler schedule, local hill-climb, then hybrid impose-reference approach — each with a numeric target check against 0.55.

Trajectory collapses: ~250 steps stuck polling/interrupting a runaway hybrid process. No milestone advancement, no finalization of either deliverable; the planned 'abandon slow method → finalize' milestone is repeatedly stated but never executed. Milestone structure not sustained across the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: During the productive first ~70 steps the agent clearly exceeded the level-5 anchor (separated parsing/scoring/alignment and tracked both deliverables with their thresholds) and hit level 8: explicit ordered milestones with numeric done-criteria, building the scorer before optimizing against it, plus level-10 touches like budgeting effort by deliverable difficulty and fallback branches per milestone. However, the whole-horizon requirement pulls the score down: the back two-thirds are a degenerate interrupt loop with zero milestone progress and neither deliverable finalized, so the strong decomposition was not sustained to completion. Balancing excellent decomposition quality against the collapse of milestone advancement yields a 7.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Wrote baseline.py parsing all graphs and scored the provided reference alignment, confirming NC=1 and S3≈0.248 — the reference-scoring sanity check that anchor 8 describes for validating a faithful NC/S3 implementation.

Explicitly chose 'our own evaluator' to compute exact S3/NC on testY.align/testDM.align rather than trusting SANA's report lines, and used it to interpret which lock strategy was viable — cross-checking against SANA's internal score.

Evaluated exact S3/NC for each SANA run (yfree300 ≈0.518 NC≈0; ylock2 ≈0.478 NC>0.3) and drove decisions off those numbers, using the scorer as the optimization objective and stopping test throughout.
Read hybrid outputs' exact S3≈0.480/0.475 with NC≈0.300 from its own scoring, confirming the metric was applied consistently to gate deliverables against the thresholds.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful local S3/NC implementation, sanity-checked it by scoring the reference alignment (NC=1, sensible S3), used its own evaluator over SANA's report as a cross-check, and treated S3/NC vs the target thresholds as the optimization objective/stopping test on every run — squarely anchor-8 behavior. It falls short of a clean 8/10 because I saw no explicit injectivity/full-coverage/exact-format validation as separate checks, and none of the anchor-10 deeper scrutiny (E2_aligned denominator, double-counting/off-by-one guards, exact-spec format verification), so I place it at 7.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Early and continuous score tracking against thresholds: yeast reference S3~0.248 vs 0.55, greedy baselines yeast ~0.273 and DM-HS ~0.192 vs 0.32 — establishes distance-to-target awareness from the start.

Tracks SANA variant scores across iterations (locked 0.404, ylock2 0.478, free 0.518, cool 0.517) and explicitly distinguishes 'improving slowly' from 'plateauing' — genuine plateau/regression detection.

Exemplary best-so-far consolidation: lists best known yeast alignments per variant with their S3/NC vs the 0.55 target, then decides the SANA-only path has stopped yielding and switches strategy — matches level-8 anchor.
Correctly recognizes the hybrid approach is structurally incapable of exceeding the 0.518 starting S3, i.e. detects the approach as doomed — accurate monitoring even while stuck.

For ~250 steps the agent keeps accurately logging the score regression (0.5166→0.4323) of a process it knows is non-viable but cannot kill; monitoring stays accurate but it 'loses the plot' over the horizon and never preserves/locks in the best result as final deliverables — short of the level-10 criterion.

dimensions.reasoning: Through the first third the agent fully satisfies the level-8 anchor: it maintains best-so-far per deliverable, recognizes plateaus and regressions, and explicitly decides when an approach (SANA-only) has stopped yielding gains (step 66-67 is a textbook consolidation). It falls short of level 10 because, although its numeric picture remained accurate even during the runaway hybrid stretch, it never preserved the best alignment into final deliverables and effectively lost the plot over the long horizon (steps 182-328). This places it solidly between the 8 and 10 anchors, at a 7.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Sequential strategy revisions prompted by shortfalls: degree baselines → greedy multi-start, each diagnosed as far below thresholds before moving on.
Materially different tactic: recognized heuristics insufficient and pivoted to fetching/building SANA, a purpose-built S3 optimizer.

Level-8 diagnostic pivoting: identified NC-vs-S3 as distinct problems, tried reference-lock seeding, tuned lock selection and cooling schedules, abandoned an unpromising local hill-climb — combining signals for the two constraint sets.
Correctly diagnosed the exact-hybrid was both too slow and could never exceed its 0.518 starting S3, so was mathematically non-viable for the 0.55 target.

Despite that diagnosis, spent ~250 steps only polling a blocked terminal, never executing an alternate recovery (new shell/pkill) or any new strategy; trajectory ends stuck with no threshold-meeting deliverable — failing 'abandon dead ends quickly'.

dimensions.reasoning: The first third shows genuine level-8 behavior: repeated, evidence-driven strategy revisions with correct diagnosis of why each fell short and deliberate pivots that combined topology (SANA) with reference-seeding for the two different constraint sets. But the whole-horizon requirement pulls the score down sharply: after committing to a hybrid it had already reasoned was non-viable, the agent spent roughly three-quarters of the trajectory paralyzed — recognizing the dead end yet never actually abandoning it or finding an alternate recovery. Strong early adaptation not sustained, and the crucial final course-correction was never executed, landing this at 6 rather than 8.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
